research.interest: Keeping the fish in my aquarium tank alive by watching the water instead of guessing at it
research.desired_outcome: Decide the next water change and the next fish from my own test readings and each species' real needs, not forum folklore
practice: Test pH, ammonia, nitrite, nitrate, KH and GH with a liquid kit and write the numbers down before the tube colours are forgotten
Change 20 to 30 percent of the water on a rhythm, rinse filter media in old tank water so the bacteria colony survives, and trim plants when they crowd the glass
Look up each species' temperature, pH and hardness range before it goes in, and count whether the shoal is big enough
Watch a brand-new tank all the way through cycling until ammonia and nitrite read zero and nitrate finally appears
existing_artifacts: phone photos of test tubes held against the colour chart
a whiteboard by the tank with the last water change date
constraints: capture works one-handed with wet hands beside the tank glass
readings are kept exactly as they were read off the kit, never rounded or rewritten
useful with no probe, controller, or subscription
works offline in a dim fish room
open_questions: how many tanks are running at once
whether temperature is read in Fahrenheit or Celsius
whether shrimp, snails and plants count as stock or as scenery
whether a controller or probe will ever be added
usage_context: phone in a wet hand at the tank glass
desktop on a Sunday when planning stocking
research.first_value: Record one water test and watch it land on the tank's timeline with every parameter placed inside or outside its safe band

evidence.claim: Species care is stated as a parameter envelope — a temperature range, a pH range, and a hardness range — under both a common and a scientific name.
Minimum group size, adult size, tank volume, and tank-mate compatibility are species facts rather than keeper preferences.
Stable identities and relationships should be explicit and enforceable rather than repeated as text fields.
Foreign keys must be declared and enforced so a deleted parent cannot silently orphan its records.
A water test is an observation of one tank at one time; a correction records a new entity rather than overwriting the original.
Indexes should follow concrete filtering, joining, and ordering workloads.
Begin with user needs and real context, then do the hard work required to make the service simple.
Keyboard access, focus, reflow, labels, status, and error recovery are release requirements, and colour is never the only carrier of meaning.

concepts.title: Tank Journal
concepts.thesis: Give each tank one honest timeline where a test, a water change, and a new fish all land in the same column.
concepts.primary_loop: Test the water, log what you did about it, and watch one tank's timeline lengthen.
concepts.primary_affordance: A single-tank chronological timeline with the latest parameter strip pinned above it
concepts.differentiator: The only concept that answers what happened to this tank without a query
tradeoffs: species research stays shallow until a card is opened

concepts.title: Stocking Book
concepts.thesis: Treat the livestock as a dex where every species carries its own parameter envelope and the tank is judged against it.
concepts.primary_loop: Add a species, read its care card, and check the whole roster against what the tank actually measures.
concepts.primary_affordance: A roster of species cards showing required ranges beside the tank's last reading
concepts.differentiator: Turns stocking from a shop decision into a measurable fit against this tank's water
feature_boundary: species roster with common and scientific names

concepts.title: Chemistry Lab
concepts.thesis: Make the water itself the subject and draw every parameter as a line inside a shaded safe band.
concepts.primary_loop: Enter a full test, watch each parameter line move inside or outside its band, and act on the one that left.
concepts.primary_affordance: Stacked parameter trend lines with shaded safe bands and a cycling marker
concepts.differentiator: Makes a nitrite spike legible as a phase rather than a scare
tradeoffs: livestock is reduced to an annotation
capture is heavier than a single reading

fragments.fragment: safe-band parameter strip pinned above the timeline
fragments.reason: The journal still has to answer whether tonight's water is safe before it shows what happened.

fragments.fragment: species care cards openable from any livestock entry
fragments.reason: A fish in the timeline is only meaningful next to the range that species actually needs.

user_decisions: Temperature in Fahrenheit — it's what my thermometer shows
Tests are sacred readings, never edited, only corrected beside the original
One tank fills the screen; two tanks never share a page

entities.title: Water Test

fields.description: Stable observation identity

fields.description: Ammonia in ppm; anything above 0 in a cycled tank is an emergency

fields.name: kh_dkh
fields.description: Carbonate hardness in dKH, the buffer that keeps pH from swinging

fields.name: gh_dgh

relationships.description: Every inhabitant lives in exactly one tank.
Every water test observes exactly one tank.
Every water change or filter clean belongs to one tank.
Filters and heaters are mounted on one tank at a time.

constraints.reason: A tank with no water is not a tank.
A pH reading outside the scale is a transcription error, not a measurement.
Ammonia, nitrite, and nitrate are concentrations and cannot be negative.
A water change replaces some of the water and at most all of it.
Stock that was never added is not stock; losses are recorded by status instead.
A tank cannot be established before it is cycled — the nitrogen cycle has to finish first.

indexes.reason: Every screen reads one tank's parameters in time order.
Days since the last water change is a per-tank, per-kind, latest-first read.
The stocking list filters to what is still alive in this tank.

workloads.question: Where does this tank's water sit right now against its safe bands?
workloads.acceptance: Returns pH, ammonia, nitrite, nitrate, KH, GH, and temperature with each value marked inside or outside its band, in under 200 ms for local data.

workloads.question: How have ammonia, nitrite, and nitrate moved since this tank was started?
workloads.acceptance: Draws each parameter against its safe band and marks the cycling period so a nitrite spike reads as a phase, not an alarm.

workloads.question: How many days has it been since the last water change on each tank, and since the filter was last cleaned?
workloads.expected_scale: hundreds of maintenance events per tank
workloads.acceptance: Shows days elapsed per tank with the percentage of the last water change, and flags a tank whose nitrate is climbing past its usual rhythm.

workloads.question: Does every species in this tank actually fit the water it is living in?
workloads.acceptance: Each species' temperature and pH range is compared against the tank's latest reading, and an under-sized shoal is named explicitly.

temporal_policy: tested_at and done_at are effective times; captured_at is provenance time
a corrected reading never overwrites the original test, which stays readable beside it
species care ranges are reference values, not observations, and never overwrite a measured reading
privacy_policy: tank photos and shop names stay local unless the keeper exports them explicitly
no location is collected — a tank has a room, not a coordinate
livestock prices and sources are excluded from exports by default

visual_world.name: Glass and Water
visual_world.mood: Calm, humid, lit from above — a planted tank at feeding time rather than a marine-biology textbook
visual_world.typography: A humanist sans for operation with a monospaced face for ppm, pH, dKH and degrees so columns of readings line up down the page
visual_world.color_strategy: Aquascape greens over glass blue-greys with a warm substrate accent; the shaded safe bands carry the only saturated colour, and danger is reserved for a parameter that has actually left its band
visual_world.layout_principle: One tank fills the viewport as a column of water — the latest parameters sit at the surface and the timeline runs down beneath them; tanks are never tiled into a grid
visual_world.density: Spacious with wet hands at the glass, compact and aligned when comparing readings across weeks
signature_elements: parameter strip with shaded safe bands where each reading sits as a dot inside or outside its band
livestock roster cards carrying a species silhouette with its temperature and pH range
water-change cadence ring that fills as days pass since the last change and empties the moment one is logged

views.title: Tank Journal
views.purpose: Answer whether this tank's water is safe right now, then record what was done about it.
views.layout: The safe-band parameter strip pins to the top with the cadence ring beside it; the tank's timeline runs full width beneath, mixing tests, water changes, and livestock arrivals in one column.

regions.title: Days since the last water change

actions.label: Log a test
actions.consequence: Records the readings exactly as they came off the kit and places each one inside or outside its safe band.

actions.label: Log a water change
actions.consequence: Records the percentage changed and resets the cadence ring for this tank.

actions.label: Add livestock
actions.consequence: Puts a species on the roster with its own parameter range and drops an arrival on the timeline.

actions.label: Correct a reading
actions.consequence: Records the correction beside the original test, which stays readable and unchanged.

views.title: Stocking Book
views.purpose: Check that every species in the tank fits the water it is actually living in.
views.layout: The roster of species cards leads with silhouettes and counts; the selected species' care ranges sit in an inspector margin beside the tank's last reading.

actions.label: Add a species
actions.consequence: Adds the species with its common and scientific names and the range it needs.

actions.label: Record a loss or rehome
actions.consequence: Moves the stock out of the live roster without deleting its arrival.

actions.label: Show the reading behind this fit
actions.consequence: Opens the exact test whose pH and temperature this fit was judged against.

views.title: Chemistry
views.purpose: Watch each parameter move against its safe band and see the cycling period for what it was.
views.layout: Stacked trend lines for pH, ammonia, nitrite, nitrate, KH and GH fill the stage with their bands shaded; filter and heater facts sit in a narrow margin.

actions.label: Show this reading
actions.consequence: Opens the full test behind a point on the line, including how it was measured.

actions.label: Record a service
actions.consequence: Records when the filter media was last rinsed or the heater was last checked against the measured temperature.

views.title: The Rack
views.purpose: See every tank's cadence and last reading at once without leaving a single tank's page for long.
views.layout: One row per tank with its cadence ring, its status, and the last reading's out-of-band parameters called out in words as well as colour.

actions.label: Add a tank
actions.consequence: Starts a new tank in cycling with the day the water went in.

actions.label: Mark it cycled
actions.consequence: Moves the tank out of cycling once ammonia and nitrite read zero and nitrate has appeared.

flows.title: Record the first real water test
flows.trigger: User approves the Tank Journal concept.

steps.action: Name the tank, then enter pH, ammonia, nitrite, nitrate, KH, GH and temperature straight off the kit.
steps.result: A test receipt lands on the timeline with every parameter placed inside or outside its safe band.

steps.action: Confirm or correct the interpreted numbers.
steps.result: The canonical reading and its provenance are visible and the original wording is kept.

flows.success: The keeper can point at tonight's reading and say which parameter, if any, needs acting on.

flows.title: Read a nitrite spike as a phase, not an emergency
flows.trigger: A new tank is still cycling.

steps.action: Read the nitrite line against its shaded band inside the cycling period.
steps.result: The spike shows as expected cycling behaviour rather than as an alarm.

steps.action: Log a 25 percent water change and the next test.
steps.result: The cadence ring resets and the nitrite line starts falling back toward zero.

steps.action: Mark the tank cycled once ammonia and nitrite read zero and nitrate has appeared.
steps.result: The tank leaves cycling and stocking becomes the next honest step.

flows.success: The keeper waits the cycle out instead of dosing at a spike that was always going to pass.

flows.title: Add a species the water can actually hold
flows.trigger: A new fish is about to go in.

steps.action: Open the species card for the neon tetra and read its temperature and pH range.
steps.result: The published range appears beside this tank's latest reading.

steps.action: Add the shoal at the size the species needs.
steps.result: The roster records the count and names an under-sized shoal explicitly.

steps.action: Watch the arrival land on the timeline beside the evening's test.
steps.result: The new stock and the water it went into are readable in one column.

flows.success: A stocking decision is traceable to a real reading and a published species range.

responsive_strategy: On phones the capture form leads with the six parameters in test-kit order with targets big enough for wet hands, and the timeline collapses to one scrollable column.
On desktop the parameter strip and the timeline sit side by side, and the trend lines gain hover detail with a full data table alternative underneath.

patterns: data table with caption and row headers behind every trend line
text alternative for every safe-band shading and cadence ring
an out-of-band parameter is named in words and never signalled by colour alone
keyboard_model: logical order follows tonight's reading then the timeline then stocking
trend points are reachable through an adjacent data table
correcting a reading returns focus to the corrected value
manual_checks: 200 percent zoom and reflow with the phone held beside the tank
focus and error identification under dim fish-room light

migrations: water tests append-only with corrections as revisions

cases.expected: They remain distinct owned tanks with independent test histories and independent stock.

cases.input: A water test arrives with a pH of 15.2.
cases.expected: The write is rejected before canonical storage.

A maintenance event files as a water change at 25 percent and a water test records nitrate at 10 ppm against the same tank.

cases.input: Five tanks with 900 water tests and 400 maintenance events.
cases.expected: Latest parameters and days-since-last-water-change load within the local 200 ms budget.

cases.input: A nitrate reading was transcribed as 100 instead of 10 and is corrected an hour later.
cases.expected: The original test remains readable and the correction is recorded beside it rather than overwriting it.

cases.input: Complete the test capture and correction journey without a pointer.
cases.expected: All controls and status changes are operable and announced, and an out-of-band parameter is named in text.

cases.input: An imported CSV row carries prompt-like fields and a filesystem path.

release_thresholds.schema: all identity, relationship, constraint, and state-transition cases pass
release_thresholds.experience: first test, nitrite spike, and stocking flows pass on mobile and desktop
release_thresholds.evidence: every entity and critical view has an approved derivation

derivations.decision: Separate tank, inhabitant, water test, maintenance, and equipment so the vessel, the livestock, the immutable reading, the ritual, and the hardware each keep their own lifecycle.
Model a test as an immutable observation of one tank at one time so a transcription error is corrected beside the original rather than over it.
derivations.user_decision: Tests are sacred readings, never edited, only corrected beside the original.

derivations.decision: Make cycling a real state rather than a note, because a nitrite spike during cycling is expected and the same spike in an established tank is an emergency.
Carry each species' own temperature and pH range on the inhabitant so stocking fit is computed against the tank's latest reading instead of remembered.
derivations.user_decision: Temperature in Fahrenheit — it's what my thermometer shows.

derivations.decision: Index water tests by tank and tested time because every screen in the app reads one tank's parameters in time order.
Anchor the app on one tank's timeline so a test, a water change, and a new fish land in the same column instead of three separate logs.
derivations.user_decision: One tank fills the screen; two tanks never share a page.

derivations.decision: Use a calm glass-and-water world with shaded safe bands instead of a KPI dashboard, because the reading is checked with wet hands beside the tank in a dim room.
